reader_notes: Read by hand from the note text (dump.ts, bars 1-34), independently: no published analysis consulted. Correspondences between passages were checked note by note with a throwaway comparison script (semitone offsets of aligned notes) and by reading. The piece has two subjects that begin together at 1:1 and run four bars. x (right hand, 1:1-4:3.75): C Bb Ab G Ab F, then Db5 tied over the bar; C Bb A Bb G, E5 tied; F G Ab Bb G E Db C; Bb Ab G Ab Bb Db C Bb Ab G F E: falling sixteenths with syncopated tied notes, each bar a step or so higher, over a dominant prolongation. y (bass, 1:1-4:3.75): an octave leap F2 F3 (dotted), then sixteenths G Ab G F Eb Db C; the same from Bb2/G3 (bar 2); a rising scale C D E F G Ab Bb G F E F E (bar 3); F3, then C D E F G Ab Bb rising (bar 4). The first eighth of y (the lower note of the leap) changes at nearly every later statement (Ab, B, Eb, F#, A ...).

opening.notes: No imitation in the usual sense: nothing is answered before bar 5. The lines are invertible at the octave (x down 8, y up 15: three octaves in all). y's first note is Ab4 at 5:1, not F. The machine's '[exchange] v1 at 5:1' is right.

notes: Over 20 of the 34 bars are members of the single paradigm, and x and y are never separated for long: it is the clearest double invention of my three. Cadences are deliberately avoided until the end: every arrival within the piece falls on an inverted tonic or is reached with the bass 7-1, so is not a cadence by the protocol: f at 4:1 (bass E-F, right hand Bb4 appoggiatura), f6/4 at 5:1, f6 at 9:1, c6 at 12:1 and at 17:1, bb at 22:1 (bass C-Bb under V7), Ab6 at 24:1, f6 at 29:1. Only 15:1 (unsure, see there) and 34:1 are counted. Form: the division at 15-17 (V of c, then c) splits the piece 16 + 18 bars; the tonic return of alpha at 29 makes it rounded bipartite. The alternative, tripartite (1-16, 17-28, 29-34), is rejected because the last part is too short to be a section of comparable length. The members at 9 and 12 are each one bar of the subjects in one key and two bars a fifth higher, so together they form a rising-fifths sequence (f-c, c-g), unit 9 beats, twice; they are recorded as members because both lines are present in full for three bars.
review: Session lead, 12 October: the reader's exclusion of arrivals on an inverted tonic (V7 to i6 at 9:1, 12:1, 17:1, 29:1) is confirmed. The protocol (section 5) does not count an arrival on an inverted tonic as a cadence; 'an inverted chord' in an IAC means an inverted dominant (V6-I, V4/3-I) resolving to a root-position tonic. A revision adding these arrivals as IACs was made on request and withdrawn after this check.
